result.title: Minimal Superior Penalties: Characterising and Calibrating Decision-Aware Proper Scoring Rules
result.summary: Training a classifier means letting a validation metric decide which model is kept and when training stops. A natural requirement on that metric is superiority: every correctly classified forecast should score better than every incorrectly classified one, however close the underlying probabilities are. Neither the Brier score nor the logarithmic score satisfies this on its own. We show that superiority is governed by the separation between two endpoints -- the supremum of the score on correct predictions and the infimum on incorrect predictions -- and derive both in closed form for each score. Their difference is the infimal penalty, the greatest lower bound on the penalty needed to restore superiority. Prior work restores superiority with a penalty calibrated from the first endpoint alone; for the Brier base, our infimal penalty is smaller than that published penalty by a factor ranging from 4.00 at three classes to 2.11 at twenty. We further embed the published and infimal penalties in a one-parameter family and show that, under a single-valued tie convention, every member of the family is strictly proper. In a pre-specified two-dataset case study, mean selected-model macro-F1 rises with the penalty in the reported ten-class regimes, though not distinguishably from noise once seed/selection-mode nesting is accounted for; a fifth regime at forty-seven classes does not reproduce even this descriptive pattern. The intended no-superiority baseline is algebraically a rescaling of the family under test, so the experiment cannot attribute the observed pattern specifically to superiority. When superiority itself is the objective, any penalty strictly above the infimal value suffices; choosing a larger penalty is a separate calibration trade-off rather than a requirement for the guarantee.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究如何让 proper scoring rule 具备「优越性」——正确分类的预测得分严格优于错误分类，推导 Brier 与对数得分的端点闭式解与最小惩罚，嵌入单参数族并给出两数据集实例研究。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「正确答案的置信得分是否必然高于错误答案」的判据与 LVR 中基于 latent 置信度做停止或验证决策的问题表述相通，可能为校准这类判据提供形式化工具，但是否适用于多模态推理输出尚需核查。
